provenance.note: Brazil underwent five currency changes 1980-1994 driven by chronic/hyperinflation: Cruzeiro (to Feb 1986) -> Cruzado (Feb 1986, 1000:1) -> Cruzado Novo (Jan 1989, 1000:1) -> Cruzeiro again (Mar 1990, 1:1 renaming) -> Cruzeiro Real (Aug 1993, 1000:1) -> Real/BRL (1 Jul 1994, 2750:1 from Cruzeiro Real, via the URV transition unit). Nominal price levels across these currencies are NOT directly comparable; any cross-era nominal comparison requires redenomination factors. To sidestep this, br_savings and br_stock (Ibovespa) series in this file are built ONLY from 1994 onward (the Real era), where a single stable currency (BRL) applies throughout. cpiIndex (1980-2025) is still built continuously across all currency eras because it is composed purely from YEAR-OVER-YEAR INFLATION PERCENTAGES (IPCA), which are currency-denomination-agnostic (a % change is unaffected by how many zeros were cut from the currency) -- this is standard practice for real-terms/purchasing-power comparisons across a redenomination. IMPORTANT: Brazil experienced hyperinflation exceeding 1,000%/year in 1988-1990 and 1992-1993 (e.g. 1989: 1,972.91%, 1990: 1,620.97%, 1993: 2,477.15%) -- this is REAL historical hyperinflation, not a data error, and is intentionally NOT smoothed away.

provenance.license: Public domain (IBGE/Banco Central do Brasil official statistics)
provenance.note: Annual IPCA (Indice de Precos ao Consumidor Amplo, Brazil's official CPI, IBGE) % change, 1980-2025, same construction method as us.json/vn.json (index[y]=index[y+1]/(1+inflation[y+1]/100), base 2025=100). 1980-2024 are official annual IPCA figures as compiled by BCB/IBGE/latinometrics. 2025 is COMPUTED (not an official closed-year figure at time of writing) by compounding the 12 actual monthly IPCA % changes for Jan-Dec 2025 published by IBGE (source: AASP IPCA table, https://www.aasp.org.br/produtos-servicos/indices-economicos/mensal/ipca-ibge/), giving ~4.26% for the year -- flagged as COMPOUNDED-FROM-MONTHLY rather than an independently-published annual figure.

provenance.license: Secondary aggregators (Yahii, Mais Retorno, Dicionario Financeiro, Mobills) of official Banco Central do Brasil (BCB) poupanca (savings account) reference-rate data.
provenance.note: Uses the 'poupanca antiga' (old/grandfathered) rule: TR (Taxa Referencial) + 6%/year (~0.5%/month), which is the rule that applies to any poupanca deposit made BEFORE 4 May 2012 and continues to apply to that deposit indefinitely -- the economically correct choice for a hypothetical saver who opened an account in 1994 and held it, as opposed to the newer Selic-linked 'poupanca nova' rule (TR + 70% of Selic when Selic<=8.5%/year) that only applies to deposits made from 4 May 2012 onward. 1994 value (22.31%) covers ONLY July-December 1994 (the Plano Real / Real-currency period that year) -- this matches standard Brazilian financial-data convention (e.g. numerando.com.br, maisretorno.com both start their poupanca tables at the Plano Real launch and treat Jan-Jun 1994 Cruzeiro Real data as out of scope, consistent with this file's 1994 currency boundary). 1995-2024 are official annual accumulated rates compounded from published monthly rates. 2025 is ESTIMATED: actual Jan-Aug 2025 accumulated was 5.3982%, extrapolated to a full-year ~8.26% assuming continuation of the ~0.67%/month trend observed through Aug 2025 -- flagged as ESTIMATED/EXTRAPOLATED.

provenance.license: B3 (Brasil, Bolsa, Balcao) is the official source of record for the Ibovespa index; Wikipedia, Yahoo Finance and UOL are secondary aggregators of the same official year-end closing levels.
provenance.note: Year-end (last trading day of December) Ibovespa nominal point close, 1994-2025, price index only (no dividend reinvestment -- Ibovespa itself is not a total-return index). closes.br_stock starts at 1994 (the Real's introduction year; the Dec-1994 close of 4,353.92 already reflects redenomination of all pre-1994 Ibovespa history into BRL terms by B3 and is NOT comparable backward across the pre-1994 currency changes, which is why no pre-1994 closes are included). returns.br_stock (year-over-year % change of these closes) accordingly starts at 1995, the first full calendar year under a stable currency. All years sourced from official/near-official B3 and B3-licensed-reseller data; none interpolated.
